{"self_assessment": "Impact
I built the bottom body line of the fish (stroke 2), which is the whole lower outline from the nose to the tail fork. It was finished early, at about 1:30, so the other pieces could grow from it. I also found the stall in the top run: it went pale after the first bend. I reported it right away, and once it was fixed I confirmed that the run was dark all the way through. The final check showed all 118 of 118 dominoes falling from the start, so the judge sees the full fish outline.

Execution
I worked from the shared sketch, laying my stroke in several short builds and standing a domino back up where one needed it. After that I spent my time on close inspections of the joints and the tail area, at 1:30, 2:00, 2:15, 2:45, 3:15, 3:45 and 5:15, so problems would surface while there was still time to fix them. I also advised that the tail tips only needed to end near the other line, with no joining at the notch. That removed a risky joint. Once the build was complete, I kept my hands off it.

Collaboration
I gave the table short, clear status updates: what was dark, what was pale, and where I was looking. That let Omar and Jack carry on with the tail pieces at the right moment, once the top run was connected. I kept out of other people's work areas to avoid bumping their dominoes.

Leadership
I kept the table focused on the connected fall rather than on decoration. I called the checkpoints (the top run is through, the tail is next, then hands off) and backed the decision to stop touching the build before the push. That kept a working fish intact.", "my_share_percent": 30}
